result.note: Tests India's position as a sugar producer, the output-consumption gap and export approval, and the states where mills shut early.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about India's sugar sector, as reported in April 2026:
items: India is the world's second-largest producer of sugar.
India's expected sugar output for the season under way exceeds its annual domestic consumption.
The government had approved exports of 2 million tons of sugar, expecting a surplus.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong. India expects only 28 million tons this season against annual consumption of 29 million tons, so output falls short of demand for the second year running. The 2 million tons of exports were approved on a surplus that never arrived, and the national stockpile is now shrinking.
questions.source: The government recently greenlit 2 million tons in exports, betting on a surplus that never arrived.

questions.prompt: In April 2026, almost all sugar mills had shut down for the season weeks ahead of schedule because of poor crops in which pair of sugar-rich states?
questions.explain: Poor cane crops forced mills in Maharashtra and Karnataka to close early. As a result, India expects 28 million tons of sugar against a forecast of 31 million tons.
questions.source: In the sugar-rich states of Maharashtra and Karnataka, almost all mills have already shut down for the season weeks ahead of schedule.
